error.signature: AI tells someone fleeing a disaster in Japan to go to the nearest 'evacuation shelter,' or treats Designated Emergency Evacuation Sites (指定緊急避難場所) and Designated Evacuation Shelters (指定避難所) as interchangeable

verdict.summary: Japan legally separates two facility types after the 2011 disaster exposed the danger of treating them as one: Designated Emergency Evacuation Sites (parks, high ground, tsunami towers) are for immediate life-threatening danger and are certified per hazard type, while Designated Evacuation Shelters (schools, gyms, community centers) are for longer-term stay after the danger passes. Cabinet Office survey data shows fewer than 1 in 5 people actually understand the distinction.

dead_ends.action: Direct someone to the nearest 'evacuation shelter' by name without checking whether it is a Designated Emergency Evacuation Site (指定緊急避難場所, for immediate danger) or a Designated Evacuation Shelter (指定避難所, for longer-term stay), treating the two as the same thing
dead_ends.why_fails: A Cabinet Office survey reported by Nippon.com found only 19.8% of respondents actually understood the distinction correctly, 14.4% believed the two terms mean the same thing, and 34% weren't sure at all; after 2011, people who sheltered in facilities that had been designated only for longer-term stay - not vetted as tsunami-safe - were killed when those buildings were inundated, which is exactly why the two-tier legal designation now exists.
dead_ends.common_misconception: That 'evacuation site' and 'evacuation shelter' are interchangeable English translations of the same Japanese concept.

dead_ends.action: Assume any given designated evacuation site or shelter is certified safe for every disaster type (earthquake, tsunami, flood) rather than checking which specific hazard it is designated for
dead_ends.why_fails: Designated Emergency Evacuation Sites are certified per hazard type - a site can be designated safe for an earthquake but explicitly excluded for tsunami or flood because it sits inside an inundation zone; using the wrong one for the disaster actually occurring is the specific failure mode the post-2011 hazard-type designation system was created to prevent.

workarounds.action: When immediate danger exists, evacuate to the Designated Emergency Evacuation Site verified for the hazard actually occurring (earthquake vs tsunami vs flood have separate designations) - check the municipal hazard map in advance, since sites are marked per-hazard, not generically.

Once immediate danger has passed and evacuation orders are lifted, move to a Designated Evacuation Shelter for longer-term refuge (food, bedding, registration) instead of remaining at the emergency assembly point, which is not equipped for extended stays.

preceded_by.condition: After deciding to evacuate immediately, the next question is where to go
If a workplace becomes unsafe, the next question is which designated facility to use
